card.headline: Cyprus wins its *first Olympic medal*
card.deck: Pavlos Kontides takes silver in the Laser at London 2012, sailing at Weymouth.

card.title: The *story*
card.text: On Monday 6 August 2012, Pavlos Kontides sailed into Olympic history at Weymouth. The 22-year-old had made sure of at least silver before the final race of the Laser class. Australia's Tom Slingsby took gold and Sweden's Rasmus Myrgren bronze, and Cyprus had the first Olympic medal in its history, in any sport.

card.title: Twelve years *later*
card.text: In Marseille on 7 August 2024, Kontides finished second again, this time in the ILCA 7 (Laser), and won Cyprus's first medal of the Paris Games. Two Olympic silvers, twelve years apart.

caption:
From the archive: August 2012, Weymouth. ⛵

Pavlos Kontides won silver in the Laser class at London 2012, the first Olympic medal in Cyprus's history, in any sport. He was 22.

Twelve years later he did it again, finishing second in the ILCA 7 (Laser) at Paris 2024 in Marseille.

Where were you when Cyprus won its first Olympic medal? 🇨🇾

alt: Archive cover, August 2012: Cyprus wins its first Olympic medal. Pavlos Kontides takes silver in the Laser at London 2012, sailing at Weymouth.

The story: on Monday 6 August 2012 at Weymouth, 22-year-old Pavlos Kontides won silver in the Laser class behind Australia's Tom Slingsby, with Sweden's Rasmus Myrgren third: Cyprus's first Olympic medal in any sport.
By the numbers: age 22 at London 2012; 2 Olympic silver medals, 2012 and 2024; 2 world titles, 2017 and 2018; Cyprus flag bearer at the Rio 2016 and Tokyo 2020 opening ceremonies.

Twelve years later: in Marseille on 7 August 2024, Kontides finished second in the ILCA 7 (Laser) for Cyprus's first medal of the Paris Games. Photo: Kontides coming ashore at the Marseille Marina, by Eric Salard, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.0.
End card: more from the archive every Tuesday and Thursday.
